candidates.name: Lumen Circuit
candidates.rationale: Rotate an optical network so a living beam preserves negation, uncertainty and quantity. Light follows the actual conduit geometry; a different path changes the message. Selected because its state space adds a distinct interpreting responsibility and can be expressed as consequential game-world actions.

candidates.name: Dialog-driven interpretation desk
candidates.rationale: Rejected because it would concentrate play into reading and answer choices, repeat the old text-heavy presentation and add little mechanical distinction to the collection.

candidates.name: Generic recall challenge with a new theme
candidates.rationale: Rejected because swapping colors, vocabulary and cover art would not change the primary verb, decision topology or the evidence produced by the existing games.

sections.title: charter
sections.body: Lumen Circuit owns a specific interpreting responsibility: Rotate an optical network so a living beam preserves negation, uncertainty and quantity. Light follows the actual conduit geometry; a different path changes the message. It is one part of a five-world curriculum and does not certify a professional. Its primary verb is refract; its decision space is described below rather than inherited from a quiz template.

sections.title: audience
sections.body: Developing and working interpreters who want practical attention and meaning-transfer exercises. Sessions last roughly three to eight minutes and support mouse, touch and keyboard. English–Spanish and English–Chinese use existing terms; synthetic world instructions are labeled practice. No prior clinical or legal credential is required to explore Lumen Circuit.

sections.title: creative-direction
sections.body: Obsidian optical instruments, brushed copper sockets, deep teal mist, luminous ivory light and tiny prism caustics. The board is physical and central, with animated light packets travelling along live segments. Title art is an original crystal aperture; essential gate symbols are visual, with optional names in help. Immediate socket rotation, a short settling spring, 140 ms pulse travel between cells, warm chord on faithful arrival and a soft fractured tone on dissipation. The player should inspect a route and feel the physical consequence of a missing qualifier. Preserve this identity across title, play and result. Other games in the collection use different geometry and temporal structure; sharing the host controls must not make their worlds look or play alike.

sections.title: gameplay-loops
sections.body: A five-by-five network contains straight and elbow conduits. Rotations change connected ports. Trace a source from west to east with a visited port-state set and a 100-hop cap. Semantic gates on visited cells toggle polarity, mark uncertainty or increment quantity. A receiver accepts only the complete target tuple and a connected physical route. Solvable layouts are generated by constructing a non-self-intersecting route first, placing its gates, and scrambling rotations afterwards. Twelve chambers, initially one transformation and generous geometry, then multiple gates, longer paths and distracting branches. No timer. Three discharged pulses at a wrong receiver lose the current chamber; restart preserves the checkpoint and changes no learning estimate until a new assessed pulse. The recurring loop is input, world change, feedback, and a consequential next action. Explanatory prose stays in optional help; the world and its changing state remain the primary interface.

sections.title: state
sections.body: SceneMachine owns title, play, paused, interlude and result. Lumen Circuit's world owns its level-local entities and counters; the host owns session ID, level checkpoint, assistance, assessed-attempt IDs and settings. No timer advances while paused. Restart replaces level-local state, retaining prior evidence and the assistance flag for a repeated challenge.

sections.title: mechanics
sections.body: A five-by-five network contains straight and elbow conduits. Rotations change connected ports. Trace a source from west to east with a visited port-state set and a 100-hop cap. Semantic gates on visited cells toggle polarity, mark uncertainty or increment quantity. A receiver accepts only the complete target tuple and a connected physical route. Completion requires a real state transition through the relevant target or encounter, never clicking a generic correct-answer button. Geometric/motor scoring is separate from language assessment, and omitted or unknown meaning cannot be silently substituted.

sections.title: entities
sections.body: A five-by-five network contains straight and elbow conduits. Rotations change connected ports. Trace a source from west to east with a visited port-state set and a 100-hop cap. Semantic gates on visited cells toggle polarity, mark uncertainty or increment quantity. A receiver accepts only the complete target tuple and a connected physical route. Each entity has a stable level-local ID, CSS-pixel or grid position, type, active state and explicit owner. Draw-only particles have no collision or assessment authority. Labels name only immediate world objects; no decorative entity is counted as authored learning content.

sections.title: interactions
sections.body: Input is sampled before simulation; movement and physical collisions resolve next; semantic gate/receiver/encounter assessment resolves once per unique attempt; feedback and checkpoint persistence follow. Tap/click a conduit to rotate clockwise. Arrow keys move a visible grid focus; Space rotates. Enter or the Pulse button launches an assessed trace. Undo restores the previous rotation. A hint reveals one needed conduit and marks this chamber assisted. Paused, title and result scenes reject world actions, and a release/cancel clears held inputs before a new scene begins.

sections.title: simulation
sections.body: A five-by-five network contains straight and elbow conduits. Rotations change connected ports. Trace a source from west to east with a visited port-state set and a 100-hop cap. Semantic gates on visited cells toggle polarity, mark uncertainty or increment quantity. A receiver accepts only the complete target tuple and a connected physical route. Solvable layouts are generated by constructing a non-self-intersecting route first, placing its gates, and scrambling rotations afterwards. Use the shared fixed 60 Hz GameLoop and bounded catch-up. World positions are CSS pixels calculated from viewport layout, while grids keep discrete coordinates. A visited-state cap, finite packet/particle capacity and explicit level boundaries prevent runaway loops and unbounded accumulation.

sections.title: ai
sections.body: There is no runtime model or adaptive NPC model in Lumen Circuit. Any NPC timing, path selection or decorative motion follows deterministic seeded rules. Authoring happened in the chat under the user's explicit quota exception. Independent CLI critique is still pending and must not be represented as completed by these deterministic agents.

sections.title: levels
sections.body: Twelve chambers, initially one transformation and generous geometry, then multiple gates, longer paths and distracting branches. No timer. Three discharged pulses at a wrong receiver lose the current chamber; restart preserves the checkpoint and changes no learning estimate until a new assessed pulse. A level begins from a reproducible seed and a validated reachable construction. Onboarding introduces only one load-bearing rule before combining it with another. Replay changes topology, state and decision order, not only names or colors. An unreachable or contradictory generated level is rejected before play.

sections.title: content
sections.body: Rotate an optical network so a living beam preserves negation, uncertainty and quantity. Light follows the actual conduit geometry; a different path changes the message. Reuse the selected concept definitions and English/Spanish/Chinese terms from the existing knowledge snapshot. Synthetic world messages are authored practice, not medical advice or jurisdiction-universal law. Missing target-language terms are shown as missing, never replaced by an unrelated language.

sections.title: difficulty
sections.body: Difficulty and evidence eligibility remain deterministic engine-core policy. Twelve chambers, initially one transformation and generous geometry, then multiple gates, longer paths and distracting branches. No timer. Three discharged pulses at a wrong receiver lose the current chamber; restart preserves the checkpoint and changes no learning estimate until a new assessed pulse. Level escalation changes interacting gameplay constraints; it does not overwrite mastery estimates. Comfort mode removes unnecessary time pressure and logs assistance where it changes assessment. Motor success alone cannot promote language difficulty.

sections.title: progression
sections.body: Lumen Circuit follows the meaning-attention foundation and prepares drift-archive. Every game remains explorable as a local experiment. Level checkpoints guide continuation; no fake stars or automatic evidence are awarded for title, help, reading, settings, pause, restart or result views.

sections.title: narrative
sections.body: The player is a carrier of meaning inside an original abstract world. Rotate an optical network so a living beam preserves negation, uncertainty and quantity. Light follows the actual conduit geometry; a different path changes the message. There are no borrowed characters, commercial artwork or claims that fictional cases happened. Narrative is expressed through the world's state and responses rather than long dialogue; source-specific professional content remains a reference boundary.

sections.title: controls-camera
sections.body: Tap/click a conduit to rotate clockwise. Arrow keys move a visible grid focus; Space rotates. Enter or the Pulse button launches an assessed trace. Undo restores the previous rotation. A hint reveals one needed conduit and marks this chamber assisted. Layout uses actual CSS viewport dimensions, with world reflow and targets around 44 pixels or larger rather than a shrunken desktop canvas. The camera shows the next consequential action. Keyboard focus is drawn in the world, and touch controls provide alternatives to precision dragging or held mouse gestures.

sections.title: ui-ux
sections.body: Open on a full-screen art-directed title for Lumen Circuit, with one primary Play/Continue action. During play, the world occupies at least 80% of the viewport; the source is one short utterance, and HUD shows only level, immediate state and essential tools. Definitions, citations, full controls and production limitations live in optional help, not stacked model-text cards.

sections.title: art
sections.body: Obsidian optical instruments, brushed copper sockets, deep teal mist, luminous ivory light and tiny prism caustics. The board is physical and central, with animated light packets travelling along live segments. Title art is an original crystal aperture; essential gate symbols are visual, with optional names in help. Author original local SVG title layers and draw interactive geometry/entities live on canvas. Never bake authoritative text, the complete HUD or the game itself into an image. Essential objects use distinct shape and motion as well as color, and asset failure has an explicit recoverable title fallback.

sections.title: animation-vfx
sections.body: Immediate socket rotation, a short settling spring, 140 ms pulse travel between cells, warm chord on faithful arrival and a soft fractured tone on dissipation. The player should inspect a route and feel the physical consequence of a missing qualifier. Draw a bounded particle pool, eased transitions and short state cues. Reduced motion removes shake, trails and nonessential parallax while retaining necessary position/state feedback. Animation never delays assessment or hides a control; draw order is background, world, agents, feedback, focus and HUD.

sections.title: audio
sections.body: Bundle original build-time rendered WAV cues and a restrained ambient score appropriate to this identity: Immediate socket rotation, a short settling spring, 140 ms pulse travel between cells, warm chord on faithful arrival and a soft fractured tone on dissipation. The player should inspect a route and feel the physical consequence of a missing qualifier. AudioMixer unlocks after the first gesture, exposes mute and volume, and keeps play functional in silence. Musical cues are feedback rather than a claim of synthesized speech or spoken-source assessment.

sections.title: accessibility
sections.body: Keyboard and touch have complete control parity. Tap/click a conduit to rotate clockwise. Arrow keys move a visible grid focus; Space rotates. Enter or the Pulse button launches an assessed trace. Undo restores the previous rotation. A hint reveals one needed conduit and marks this chamber assisted. Provide visible focus, readable source text, shape-coded state, a pause affordance, reduced motion, mute/volume and comfort mode. Blur cancels input and opens pause; returning cannot silently resume an active timer. Help explains exact controls and the limited learning responsibility.

sections.title: architecture
sections.body: Use one shared host for lifecycle, assets, audio, input, persistence and validated multi-domain EngineClient instances, plus a separate lumen-circuit world module implementing its own state space and rules. The host imports actual engine-core and game-runtime APIs. Rendering has no authority to update learning state, and worlds never duplicate mastery or retention math.

sections.title: performance
sections.body: Target 60 Hz on desktop and mobile with DPR capped at two, finite entities and bounded effects. A five-by-five network contains straight and elbow conduits. Rotations change connected ports. Trace a source from west to east with a visited port-state set and a 100-hop cap. Semantic gates on visited cells toggle polarity, mark uncertainty or increment quantity. A receiver accepts only the complete target tuple and a connected physical route. Solvable layouts are generated by constructing a non-self-intersecting route first, placing its gates, and scrambling rotations afterwards. Avoid per-frame DOM rebuilds and runtime network dependencies. Fixed-step catch-up drops excess time rather than fast-forwarding an invisible world. Large source/reference prose is loaded only for optional reading, not every frame.

sections.title: persistence
sections.body: VersionedStore keeps the level checkpoint, seed, settings, best local run and assistance markers. EngineClient separately owns append-only domain-isolated evidence. Reload resumes the current level, not a fabricated exact-frame snapshot. Corrupt data resets safely; blocked/quota storage leaves play possible and exposes exportable in-session progress.

sections.title: generation
sections.body: A five-by-five network contains straight and elbow conduits. Rotations change connected ports. Trace a source from west to east with a visited port-state set and a 100-hop cap. Semantic gates on visited cells toggle polarity, mark uncertainty or increment quantity. A receiver accepts only the complete target tuple and a connected physical route. Solvable layouts are generated by constructing a non-self-intersecting route first, placing its gates, and scrambling rotations afterwards. Seeds determine topology, content order and timing. Generate a valid solution or feasible schedule first, scramble the presentation second, then validate reachability and resource budgets. Do not claim variation from color/name swaps. Failed validation regenerates within a bounded attempt count or reports an explicit error.

sections.title: testing
sections.body: Exercise a full Twelve chambers, initially one transformation and generous geometry, then multiple gates, longer paths and distracting branches. No timer. Three discharged pulses at a wrong receiver lose the current chamber; restart preserves the checkpoint and changes no learning estimate until a new assessed pulse. Test keyboard and portrait touch, pause/blur, restart, hint persistence, seeded replay, repeated completion, malformed storage, missing audio, and the distinction between motor errors and assessed meaning errors. Logic tests cover reachable solutions and finite event ordering; real browser play is separately recorded.

sections.title: acceptance
sections.body: A complete session in Lumen Circuit must be reachable through actual world actions, with escalation, meaningful consequence, win/result, recoverable failure and replay. The saved definition, required assets, lifecycle controls and shared evidence integration must exist. Independent CLI design/code reviews remain pending; do not mark a model or human quality gate passed merely because files compile.

sections.title: delivery
sections.body: Deliver a static standalone package for lumen-circuit: index, style, source modules, bundled art/audio, knowledge snapshot, shared learning/runtime modules, this framework and an honest acceptance report. Include it in the local learning hub as an experiment. The author can hide/remove it easily; no automatic publication follows a successful build.

sections.title: risks
sections.body: Risks include a motor or routing solution that bypasses the meaning task, a dominant waiting strategy, repeated-seed farming, tiny mobile targets, source ambiguity and overclaiming evidence. Rotate an optical network so a living beam preserves negation, uncertainty and quantity. Light follows the actual conduit geometry; a different path changes the message. Keep the assessed responsibility narrow and inspect real play. Aesthetic ambition does not waive state correctness or the still-pending independent critiques.

sections.title: traceability
sections.body: Trace WORLD-lumen-circuit to the unique refract loop, SOURCE-interpreting-skill-4 to the reused knowledge, LIFE-01 to host scenes, ACCESS-01 to keyboard/touch, SAVE-01 to checkpoint recovery and EVIDENCE-01 to the assessed-action event. Every advertised feature needs actual code and observed or tested evidence; limitations remain explicit in the build report.
